messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: latency SLA breach detected for pool=GPU-SHARED-1 route=/v1/generate. p95 jumped to 1.3s, p99 =~ 6.8s, streaming stalls observed. window start=1772008970. Affected customers: ACME (high), GlueLabs (medium). Auto-escalation to on-call.

leah: ack — i'm oncall, paging triage now. any evidence of rolling deploys? @sanjay can you pull grafana and k8s? :eyes: 

sanjay: looking. no deploys in the last 30m. graphs show sudden tail latency bump ~1772008950. CPU low, GPU util high on some nodes, and disk iowait spikes. correlating to large checkpointing jobs from multi-tenant pods. pulling node list.

maria: streaming stalls look like long KV cache loads + IO stalls. checking runtime logs for stalls/lock contention. also seeing many retransmits from grpc streams.

leah: can we identify noisy tenant pod(s)? priority = find culprit and either evict or throttle to restore SLOs. 

sanjay: found suspicious pods on node gpu-node-7: `tenant-id=usage-peak-42` — multiple pods launching heavy model-owners (large sequence lengths). Top processes: model loader memory-mapped checkpoints causing disk reads. nvidia-smi snapshot: 
```
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used --format=csv,noheader
75 %, 82 %, 11232 MiB
95 %, 90 %, 21500 MiB  <-- gpu-node-7
```

sanjay: iostat shows high sda read/write: 
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
sda 12.00 450.00 2048 92160 0.00 0.00 12.34 120.50 2.10 118.40 0.20 92.00
```

ow: heavy disk activity aligning with tail. likely checkpoint writes/reads from ephemeral storage.

ow: attempted quick check `kubectl top pod -n inference --sort-by=memory` shows `usage-peak-42-` pods at top memory.

leah: plan: 1) throttle/evict noisy tenant 2) fallback some traffic to dedicated pool 3) increase cgroup memory limit? 4) notify support for customer impact. anyone object?

maria: i can initiate a soft-eviction: scale the tenant's replica count to 0 with graceful drain, and re-route its new traffic to dedicated-spot if needed. will also add a QoS cgroup to limit IO. 

ow: executing: `kubectl scale deploy usage-peak-42 -n inference --replicas=0` — going to cordon pods on gpu-node-7 for rebalancing, then remove from service.

ow: applied QoS throttle on node: `echo 120000 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/blkio.throttle.read_iops_device` (applied to tenant's cgroup) — reducing IO rate.

ow: immediate telemetry update: p99 dropped from 6.8s -> 3.2s, p95 1.3s -> 900ms. streaming stalls down but not fully back to baseline.

leah: good. start moving long-running model jobs off shared pool. owen, can you spin up a small dedicated pool (dedicated-rt-2) and migrate the heavy model there? we should do a canary move.

ow: creating dedicated pool slot, provisioning 2 gpus. command: `rdwctl allocate-pool --name dedicated-rt-2 --gpus 2 --region us-west` (internal tool). 

ow: provisioning done. migrating one replica: patched service selector for usage-peak-42 to target `pool=dedicated-rt-2` for a canary. 

maria: canary warmup looks ok. latency for canary requests is stable p95 ~ 120ms. starting draining remaining pods from gpu-node-7.

sanjay: monitoring infra metrics — block IO utilization on gpu-node-7 decreased to %util 28 after eviction. streaming stalls largely resolved.

leah: support: @kelly — customer impact summary for ACME? need timeline and whether we should send postmortem-ready notice.

kelly: ACME reported token stalls and two aborted streams between 12:30-12:39 UTC (~9m window). their SLA monitors flagged errors and retried; they rerouted some traffic client-side. I'll open a support ticket and prepare an initial incident notification to ACME. ETA 15m for initial comms.

leah: handoff note: @maria will continue mitigation and follow-up on infra fixes. I'm staying on the thread for customer comms for the next 10m then handing back to ops.

maria: follow-ups: 1) apply IO cgroup limits globally on shared pool nodes; 2) add admission control to block large checkpoint jobs on shared pool; 3) telemetry alert tuning to catch early iowait rise. will file infra task and link to ticket.

ow: created internal incident INC-2026-4017 and linked this thread. runbook steps executed: noisy-tenant-evict, pool-migrate, cgroup-throttle.

ops-bot: Post-incident reminder — collect kernel logs and dmesg from gpu-node-7 and upload to INC-2026-4017.

sanjay: uploading `dmesg` snippets and `journalctl -u inference.service` to the incident. highlights: repeated page cache writeback spikes and process `model_loader` reading large checkpoint files in small random IO pattern — causing high avg. await.

maria: temporary mitigation successful. next steps assigned: owen -> automation to detect checkpoint IO by label, sanjay -> recommend default cgroup blkio policy, leah -> customer comms and postmortem lead, kelly -> customer-facing ticket + RCA summary.

leah: closing notes before handoff: SLO restored to target for public routes, dedicated migration prevented recurrence for this tenant. major risk remains without admission controls — we'll treat that as priority P1 backlog item. Thanks team. :heart:

ops-bot: Incident state updated to "mitigated". last_action_ts=1772009300.
